title: Rock al Parque Unveils Full 2026 Lineup Featuring Ministry, Editors, Mon Laferte and More
summary: The free festival will celebrate three decades at Bogotá's Parque Simón Bolívar with more than 60 performers.
contentText:
Rock al Parque has finalized the lineup for its historic 30th anniversary edition. The free Colombian festival will return to Bogotá’s Parque Simón Bolívar from Oct. 10-12 with a program featuring international acts such as Los Bunkers (Chile), Editors (England), Mon Laferte (Chile/Mexico), Ministry (USA), Apocalyptica (Finland), Rata Blanca (Argentina) and Porter (Mexico).

The announcement, made on Wednesday (Aug. 26) by the Instituto Distrital de las Artes (Idartes ), comes just over a week after the event unveiled its 26 local artists . The new wave of acts confirms the international scope of the celebration, with alternative rock, metal, punk, ska, reggae and other related sounds spread across four stages.

The lineup also includes the iconic power metal band Stratovarius (Finland), alongside Between the Buried and Me, Algiers and Darkest Hour from the U.S.; Grave and Hellbutcher from Sweden; as well as Burning Witches and Triptykon with Hellhammer and Celtic Frost from Switzerland. Also featured are Japan’s Tokyo Ska Paradise Orchestra, Venezuelan group Desorden Público, Chile’s Gondwana and Spain’s Green Valley and Iseo & Dodosound.

Plus, Argentina’s Bandalos Chinos, Ratones Paranoicos and Serú Girán; Mexico’s División Minúscula and Las Fokin Biches; Chile’s Los Tetas, Claudio Narea and Decessus; as well as Uruguay’s Trotsky Vengarán. Representing Colombia, Esteman, I.R.A. and Nadie, among others, will also be present.

Founded in 1995, Rock al Parque has established itself as one of the largest free open-air festivals in Latin America. For its 2026 edition, the event will celebrate three decades of history with a mix of international icons, Latin American artists and a broad showcase of Bogotá’s local scene.
